topic: Google Cloud Professional Agentic Architect certification exam preparation - Google Cloud's brand-new professional certification for designing, building, evaluating, deploying, securing, and governing AI agents and multi-agent systems on Google Cloud, centered on Vertex AI Agent Builder, the Agent Development Kit (ADK), Agentspace/Gemini Enterprise, and Gemini models
exam_format: Approximately 80 multiple choice and multiple select questions, 3 hours, delivered online-proctored or at an onsite test center. Registration is 200 USD plus applicable tax (a 120 USD beta price applied during the beta window). The credential uses a two-part structure: Part 1 is the proctored multiple-choice exam covering conceptual knowledge, system design, and architectural standards; Part 2 is a set of hands-on labs in Google Skills that validate execution and coding ability, taken after passing Part 1. No prerequisites; Google recommends 3+ years of hands-on cloud experience including 1+ years building agentic solutions on Google Cloud. Passing score is not publicly published by Google. The exam went to general availability with GA registration opening November 2, 2026 (built during the beta period).
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) and multiple select clearly marked as 'Select TWO/THREE'
audience: Cloud architects, AI engineers, and application developers who design and deploy production AI agents and multi-agent systems on Google Cloud. Candidates should have solid Google Cloud and Vertex AI experience plus at least a year building agentic solutions, and comfort with Python and generative AI concepts. A strong next step up from the Google Cloud Generative AI Leader and Professional ML Engineer courses in this catalog.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Build agents using low-code tools
domains.notes: Designing and building agents with Google Cloud's low-code/no-code agent tooling: Vertex AI Agent Builder, Agentspace / Gemini Enterprise agent experiences, Conversational Agents (Dialogflow CX) and data-store/search agents, playbooks and goal-based flows. Connecting agents to enterprise data sources and grounding with Vertex AI Search. Knowing when a low-code builder is the right choice versus a custom-coded agent, and the limits of managed builders. Configuring tools, knowledge, and guardrails without writing orchestration code.

domains.name: Use coding agents for application development
domains.notes: Using AI coding assistants and coding agents (Gemini Code Assist, Gemini CLI, agentic IDE workflows) to accelerate application development. Prompting and steering coding agents, reviewing and validating generated code, integrating coding agents into the SDLC and CI/CD, and the responsible-use and security considerations of agent-generated code. Understanding where coding agents fit in an agentic architecture and how architects enable teams to use them safely and productively.

domains.name: Develop custom agents
domains.notes: The core technical domain. Building custom and multi-agent systems with the Agent Development Kit (ADK) and the Vertex AI Agent Engine runtime: agent roles and goals, tool and function calling, memory and session/state management, retrieval-augmented grounding, planning and multi-step reasoning. Orchestrating multi-agent patterns (sequential, parallel, hierarchical/orchestrator-worker, routing), agent-to-agent communication and interoperability (A2A protocol, MCP tool integration), model selection across Gemini variants, and connecting agents to APIs, databases, and enterprise systems. Choosing the right framework, runtime, and orchestration pattern for a described requirement.

domains.name: Evaluate and deploy agentic workflows
domains.notes: Evaluating agent quality and reliability: trajectory and tool-use evaluation, response/groundedness/safety metrics, the Vertex AI evaluation service, offline vs online evaluation, human-in-the-loop review, and detecting hallucination and tool-misuse. Deploying and operationalizing agents: Agent Engine deployment, scaling, versioning, observability/tracing, token and latency/cost analysis, and CI/CD for agents. Choosing deployment targets and evaluation strategies for a described SLA, budget, and risk profile.

domains.name: Secure and govern agentic workflows
domains.notes: Securing agents and multi-agent systems: identity and least-privilege access for agents (service accounts, IAM, delegated/agent identity), securing tools and data access, prompt-injection and tool-abuse defenses, data exfiltration and output-handling controls, VPC Service Controls and network isolation, and secrets/credential management. Governance and responsible AI for agents: guardrails and policy enforcement, approval and oversight modes for autonomous actions, audit logging and provenance, Model Armor / safety filters, and compliance considerations. Choosing the correct security control or governance pattern for a described agentic scenario.

extra_guidance: This is a BRAND-NEW, high-demand certification and a first-to-market opportunity - the marketing angle is 'the first complete prep for Google's new Professional Agentic Architect, built for the agentic-AI era', and the funnel is the technical step up from the Google Cloud Generative AI Leader course and a peer to the Professional ML Engineer course in this catalog. ACCURACY note: the five domain NAMES above are taken verbatim from Google's published beta exam guide; Google does NOT publish official percentage weightings, so the percentages above are our editorial distribution reflecting the exam's emphasis (custom agents + build/evaluate/deploy are the heaviest) - present the domain names as official but do NOT claim the percentages are Google's figures. Because this was authored during the beta window, add a one-line note in chapter 1 that candidates should confirm the current exam guide on the official Google Cloud certification page (the guide may be refined at GA on November 2, 2026), and re-scan the config against the final GA exam guide before marketing. Vertex AI Agent Builder, the Agent Development Kit (ADK), Agent Engine, Agentspace/Gemini Enterprise, and Gemini models are the through-line of the entire exam; emphasize agent orchestration patterns, tool/function calling, grounding, evaluation, and agent security/governance. This is a design and decision exam - practice questions MUST be scenario/case-study based with 'best Google Cloud service / most secure / most cost-effective / most scalable agent design' framing and plausible distractors. Hammer the classic decision pairs: low-code Agent Builder vs custom ADK, single-agent vs multi-agent orchestration patterns, Agent Engine vs self-managed runtime, RAG/Vertex AI Search grounding choices, evaluation strategy selection, and agent security controls (IAM/agent identity, Model Armor, prompt-injection defenses, VPC-SC). Labs are Google Cloud console and ADK read-and-understand walkthroughs (build an Agent Builder agent, wire a tool, deploy to Agent Engine, run an evaluation, apply a guardrail), not deep gcloud memorization - and note the real cert includes a Part 2 hands-on lab component so the course should prepare learners for applied tasks, not just MCQs. Final chapter must be a full exam simulation with a 3-hour / ~80-question time-management strategy and multiple-response elimination guidance. Scan the practice bank for other-vendor terms (AWS/Azure) before upload per the pipeline compliance rules.
